title: Fix SoftBody3D pinned_points editing bugs
body:
Editing the `pinned_points` array of a SoftBody3D triggered three bugs:

1. Increasing the last element deleted the pin and printed "Invalid index for pin point insertion position." The insertion-position guard in `pin_point()` rejected `p_insert_at == pinned_points.size()`, even though `Vector::insert` accepts a position in `[0, size()]` (inserting at `size()` is a valid append). Changed `>=` to `>`.

2/3. `_set_property_pinned_points_indices()` grabbed `pinned_points.ptrw()`
   once and then called `pin_point()`, which mutates `pinned_points` via
   `remove_at()`/`insert()` mid-loop, invalidating the pointer and changing
   `size()`. It also overloaded `-1` as a sentinel, so a user-typed `-1` was
   forwarded to the physics server (Jolt then reported it out of bounds every
   step) and was never unpinned when corrected, leaving a stale error state.

Rewrote `_set_property_pinned_points_indices()` to snapshot the old list and rebuild in a single pass, calling only `_pin_point_on_physics_server()` (which never touches `pinned_points`). Removed points are unpinned by comparing the old and new index lists; negative indices are never sent to the physics server. Attachment/offset data is preserved for points that stay pinned.
